event: "Some morning," she says. "Grand." She strips bare, pulls on her cap, and holds out her hand.
You strip to your knickers and bra, shaking already; the mere is ten degrees and black.

memory.fact: In late September the mere is about ten degrees, cold enough to take a swimmer's breath away.

event: Shiv says the trick is not to think; she counts three and you jump together, hand in hand.
The cold hits like a fist; you surface shrieking, and Shiv's hand is still in yours.

event: She holds you up, laughing, and tells you to breathe out, slow; you do, and the panic loosens.
For one long minute you tread water together, the fells pink, your whole body burning and alive.

event: She hauls you out onto the rock and wraps you in her parka, rubbing your arms hard.
Up close her wet freckled shoulders are inches from you; she sees you look, and stays close.

memory.fact: On the rock after their swim, Shiv saw Nala watching her bare shoulders, and stayed close.

event: Bea comes running along the shore at half six, sees you both, and stops dead, mouth open.
"You went IN?" Bea shrieks; you nod, teeth chattering; she swears she's telling Yusra, grinning.

event: Hot shower, the best of your life; your skin stays pink and humming all through breakfast.

event: Ten o'clock: History of Magic in the Long Room; the old guilds, then the Licensing Act of 1858.

memory.fact: Nala's Thursday: History of Magic at ten in the Long Room, and practical casting at two.
First-year History of Magic runs from the old guilds through the 1858 Act to the colleges' founding.
The Licensing Act of 1858 made working magic for pay in Britain a licensed trade, like medicine.

event: Kit comes up the benches and, after a pause, silently takes the place beside you.

memory.fact: First-year History of Magic runs from the old guilds through the 1858 Act to the colleges' founding.

event: The lecture names dates and kings you half know from Alan's history, gone strange here.

memory.fact: This world's history has the names of Alan's, Henry to Cromwell, but other dates and causes.

event: You frown at a date that's wrong to you; Kit, low, asks what's the matter; you say nothing, sorry.
Kit starts muttering asides about the lecturer's dates and the guildmasters' beards, deadpan.

memory.fact: Kit's grandmother had the same History of Magic lecturer, who has had a date wrong for forty years.

event: She's quietly, wickedly funny; you shake with held laughter; Kit's mouth stays perfectly straight.

memory.fact: Kit sat by Nala in History and murmured deadpan jokes about the lecture until Nala shook.
Kit reads poetry she would deny reading, and is quietly very funny once she trusts someone.

event: Amara, two rows down, turns to see what's funny, and her eyes narrow at Kit beside you.

memory.fact: In History, Amara turned, saw Nala shaking with laughter beside Kit, and narrowed her eyes.

event: Two o'clock: practical casting in the Practice Hall again; glims, one at a time at the front.
Amara goes first again and her glim is perfect again; the hall murmurs.
Kit is next in line; you see her hand already starting to tremble at her side.
You step out in front of her before she can move, and say you'll go, loud enough to turn heads.
Every eye in the hall swings to you, the girl who'd never cast a spell.

event: The word; the stroke, the loop, the hook curling in; you mean light with everything you have.
A light rises off your palm: small, wavering, white, and it lifts, and it hangs at your eye level.
It holds, three seconds, five, ten; your first glim; you hear Priya squeal and Shiv whoop.

event: The demonstrator sees both and says, "Ashby. Ashworth. Good." Then, to the room: "Next."

event: Your glim gutters out; the headache comes, but lighter; Lin, at the back, is beaming at you.

memory.fact: Nala's headache after her first glim was much lighter than Tuesday's.

event: Kit passes you on the way out and says, low, "You did that on purpose." You shrug.
She looks at you a long moment; "Thank you," she says; you both nearly laugh at once.

memory.fact: Kit told Nala she went first on purpose and thanked her, and both nearly laughed at the thanks.

event: Bea announces to the kitchen that you made a glim today, and makes you show everyone.
You cast it in the crowded kitchen, everyone watching; it rises, small and steady, and holds.
The kitchen cheers; Lin claps her inky hands; Yusra raises her mug to you across the room.

event: Later, the kitchen emptying, Yusra says quietly that a glim in four days from nothing is good.
"I said some take a month," she says. "You're not some." She rinses your mug for you.

memory.fact: Yusra told Nala a glim in four days from nothing is good, and that she is not one who takes a month.

event: She tells you she's kissed girls and boys both, and likes girls best, and has never been in love.

memory.fact: By Thursday Bea's half-glim had become two-thirds of a glim, by her own estimate.
Bea has kissed girls and boys both, likes girls best, and has never been in love.

event: She asks if you have; you say it's complicated, and she accepts that, watching you.

memory.fact: Asked by Bea if she had ever been in love, Nala said it's complicated, and Bea let it be.

event: She lies back across your narrow bed beside you, still talking, slower and slower.

memory.fact: Bea grew up in Bristol, the eldest of four, her mother Swedish and her father a bus driver.

event: Bea falls asleep mid-sentence, her head on your shoulder, her hair coming loose over your neck.

memory.fact: Bea fell asleep mid-sentence on Nala's bed on Thursday night, her head on Nala's shoulder.

event: You lie still, the radiator knocking, her warmth all down your side, and let her stay.
